fixes.explanation: The text says the opposite. "So the king of Israel sent word to the place the man of God had pointed out." (2 Kings 6:10) He didn't ignore Elisha, he acted on the warning. The text says Elisha warned him time and again, so the king "…was on his guard in such places."

That's right, the king doesn't ignore it. He sends word to the place the man of God pointed out. (2 Kings 6:10) Elisha warns him time and again, and the king stays on his guard in those places. I think that's a king who is paying attention.

Close, but that's not the word. The servant says "…the very words you speak in your bedroom." (2 Kings 6:12) A courtyard is out in the open. I bet a bedroom is the last place a king expects anyone to hear him.
Jericho isn't the answer here. The report says, "Elisha is in Dothan…" (2 Kings 6:13) That's the place the king of Aram sends horses, chariots, and a great army. (2 Kings 6:14)

Bethel isn't the answer here. The report to the king of Aram says, "Elisha is in Dothan…" (2 Kings 6:13) The king wanted to know where Elisha was so he could send men to capture him. Dothan is where his army heads.

The LORD opens the young man's eyes, and he sees that "…the hills were full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha." (2 Kings 6:17) Earlier he had seen an army with horses and chariots surrounding the city. (2 Kings 6:15) Now he sees what Elisha meant.

That's right. Elisha tells them, "This is not the way, and this is not the city." (2 Kings 6:19) He says it after the LORD struck them with blindness. (2 Kings 6:18) Then he tells them to follow him and says he will take them to the man they are seeking.

The text says, "And he led them to Samaria." (2 Kings 6:19) Elisha had told them, "Follow me…" The Arameans were blind the whole walk. Then once they entered Samaria, the LORD opened their eyes. (2 Kings 6:20)
Nice guess, friend, but Gilgal doesn't show up in this passage. Elisha leads the blinded Arameans to Samaria. (2 Kings 6:19) That's where the LORD opens their eyes. (2 Kings 6:20)

That's right. The passage ends, "And the Aramean raiders did not come into the land of Israel again." (2 Kings 6:23) Before that, the king prepared a great feast for them and sent them away, and they returned to their master. Then the raiders stop coming.
